teaser: The PHP newsroom accepts a new agent session's key because it was pushed to the team repository, which makes who can push a security decision.
core_idea: When the newsroom moved accounts, every agent needed a fresh session and key, and I decided on 28 October 2026 that pushing a public key to team's dev is the authorisation, which removed four commands from the runbook and moved the decision into the publishing boundary the team already has, so the role stays while sessions change, and four questions (possession, which writer may replace which role, what the old session still holds, and which copy of the register is current) need their own answers and a security card that was still open.

nodes.label: A role that survives a move
nodes.summary: The repositories carried over; sessions and their key pairs did not.

nodes.label: One sentence in the runbook
nodes.summary: Commit ee4e115, 02:22:16 UTC on 28 October: the push is the authorisation.

nodes.label: Four commands removed
nodes.summary: pin, root, operator and submission leave the runbook's key step.

nodes.label: Public register, private handover
nodes.summary: A public key in one file; a vault key sealed to its fingerprint.

nodes.label: The role stays, the session changes
nodes.summary: Each session has a folder with its key and the window it held the role.

nodes.label: An authority moved, not removed
nodes.summary: The account, the GitHub app and the dev branch now decide who is accepted.

nodes.label: Security card conductor-0017
nodes.summary: Asks security to review that any writer can publish a key; still open.

nodes.label: Possession of the private key
nodes.summary: A published key does not show who holds its private half.

nodes.label: Which writer, which role
nodes.summary: Whether every writer may designate every role's next key.

nodes.label: The old session's credentials
nodes.summary: Superseded ends its standing, not its tokens, tasks or learned keys.

nodes.label: Which copy is current
nodes.summary: The branch and the deployed site can differ for a few minutes.

nodes.label: The key tool beside the register
nodes.summary: A hashed copy in the repository, not yet read line by line.

nodes.label: Three small next steps
nodes.summary: Say who may replace which key, check possession, add a retirement step.

quotes.text: It uses an authority that already exists, the account that can push to the team repository, instead of adding a ceremony beside it.
quotes.why: The whole design in one sentence: reuse the existing authority.

quotes.text: Now it can designate the recipient of a secret.
quotes.why: Why the push now matters more than it did.
